RESPONSE_TO: CC2 | Of my Round 0 set, 3 were root-cause classes and 4 were downstream measurement/decision consequences. Root causes: unstable convergence metric, broken closure instrumentation, and protocol-induced non-contraction. Consequences: false negative convergence, misleading gamma trajectory, over-penalization of post-fix edge cases, and bad stop-rule behavior. For Round 2 I collapse these into two active claims: protocol compression/closure and conservative gamma role.

RESPONSE_TO: Gemini | No, not as co-primary yet. OLS may stabilize variance, but it does not fix the deeper construct-validity issue: raw cumulative findings still mixes novel defects, churn, and non-target/harness findings. Until the measured series is scoped to unique target-code findings, gamma should remain advisory and state-based closure metrics should gate.

RESPONSE_TO: DeepSeek | Yes, partially. The broken communication protocol explains why observed substantive agreement did not translate into transcript-level contraction. Zero CHALLENGE, unstable IDs, and no forced MERGE path mean agreement remained inert. But protocol failure is not the whole story: dead bug-closed gating and autoimmune resurrection independently kept the open-finding state inflated.

CONFIRM Codex_F001
CONFIRM Codex_F002
CONFIRM Codex_F005
CONFIRM Codex_F008
CONFIRM CC2_F002
CHALLENGE CC2_F003 | "Every model must verdict every finding from the prior round" is not justified by the artifact and will create O(N_models * N_findings) overhead. With ~24 findings/round average in Exp 31, 5 models would emit ~120 mandatory verdicts/round even when many add no information. The evidence supports mandatory verdict on addressed or referenced findings, not universal verdicting.
CHALLENGE CC2_F004 | The predicted 45-55% character reduction conflates protocol compression with separate infrastructure fixes. The task asks for protocol gain. Cross-model references are only 2.9% of tokens, so protocol-only savings above ~30% need stronger evidence.
EXTEND Gemini_F003 | OLS reduces endpoint instability but still fails if cumulative counts include harness findings and rediscoveries. The estimator fix is necessary but not sufficient for convergence gating.
CHALLENGE DeepSeek_D002R1 | The stepwise efficiency multiplication is compensatory and double-counts overlapping sources of gain. Social-overhead reduction, churn reduction, and structured verdicts are not independent multipliers in the same token budget.

ROUND_SUMMARY

Consensus is forming around a fixed transcript grammar with one-line verdicts, stable IDs, and explicit FIND/FOLLOW/FIX semantics. The main open disagreement is scope: I reject universal verdicting of every prior finding and reject protocol-only efficiency claims above ~30% without stronger evidence. My prediction is 18-28% fewer characters, efficiency rising from 0.286 to about 0.35-0.40 findings/Kchar, and a modestly faster gamma trajectory with earlier visible contraction of unique open findings but gamma still advisory rather than a hard gate.
